name: Woodland Trust (SoGive, 2020)
summary: Plants, restores and protects woodland in the UK. SoGive's estimate of what its tree planting (the Create Woodland project) costs per tonne of CO₂ taken up, from the 2019 annual report, rebuilt from SoGive's analysis.

source.title: Woodland Trust: SoGive rating and analysis
source.license: No licence on the page. SoGive's data terms (sogive.org/doc/getourdata.html, archived September 2019): data for charity analysis is free with attribution to SoGive; use in apps needs a licence, free for low-intensity use, on condition that users are told the source of impact assessments with a link back to SoGive. This model cites SoGive and links its page.

resources.title: SoGive, Woodland Trust analysis
resources.note: SoGive's charity page (its analysis text); SoGive publishes no spreadsheet for it, so the model is built from the figures stated in the text, each quoted on its row. Rated "Not Recommended (tentative)"; the record was last modified on 16 November 2020.

resources.title: Rethink Priorities, climate change versus global health interventions (2026)
resources.note: Source of the shared rate that turns tonnes into deaths.

sections.title: Create Woodland: tree planting, 2019
sections.explainer: SoGive split the Woodland Trust's 2019 spending (£53.3m) across its three projects, sharing out the £10.4m of fundraising costs in proportion.

sections.title: Restore and Protect Woodland, 2019
sections.explainer: SoGive also costs the restoration project per tonne and calls the protection project far worse without a number. Not in SoGive's headline; our view uses them, because a donation funds all three.

sections.title: From pounds per tonne taken up to tonnes per dollar
sections.explainer: charityevals' steps after SoGive's bottom line: all three projects, since a donation to the Woodland Trust isn't restricted to planting; pounds to dollars; and the decades over which the trees take up the carbon, discounted at the shared rate. The tonnes are carbon taken up by trees, not fuel left unburned, so they cut no air pollution (docs/normalization.md 2.5).

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not the evaluator's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: CO₂ taken up by a tree over 100 years (tonnes)

source.title: SoGive, charity analysis
source.quote: the average tree would have a 100-year lifespan and sequester ~2.25 tons of CO2

rows.explainer: SoGive assumes 5.9 kg of CO₂ a year for a tree's first 10 years and 22 kg a year for the next 90, and states the total as about 2.25 tonnes; those rates add up to 2.04 tonnes. SoGive's 2.25 is kept here, so its £2.14 reproduces; at 2.04 it would be £2.36. Every tree is assumed to survive and stand for 100 years.

rows.explainer: SoGive: "a Woodland Trust tree from the Create project would sequester CO2 at the rate of over £2.14/ton", against its benchmark of £1 a tonne averted.

rows.label: US dollars per pound, 2019
rows.explainer: charityevals' step: SoGive's figure is in pounds; the site counts per dollar, so the pounds are converted at the year's average exchange rate (shared fact).

rows.label: Discount rate
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate (Your values). SoGive doesn't discount, so the evaluator view pins it at 0.

rows.label: Average years until the carbon is taken up

source.title: SoGive, charity analysis
source.quote: Assuming a rate of 5.9 kg CO2 sequestered per tree per year for the first 10 years of early tree life, followed by a rate of 22 kg CO2 sequestered per tree per year for the remaining 90 years of tree life

rows.explainer: A tonne taken up decades from now does less than one kept out of the air today. At SoGive's rates a tree takes up its carbon on average 54 years after planting, a restored hectare 50 years; the low end allows for faster early growth. The site's climate conversion treats tonnes as averted now, so this delay is discounted here.

rows.label: Discount factor for the delay
Tonnes of CO₂ taken up per dollar, discounted to today
rows.explainer: One over the all-project cost per tonne in dollars, times the discount for the delay. Written through SoGive's figure so the step from its bottom line shows.

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
rows.explainer: The row the site's climate conversion reads (docs/normalization.md 2.5): the air-pollution deaths each of these tonnes avoids, as a multiple of the world average behind the shared rate, 1.46 air-pollution deaths per 10,000 tonnes of CO₂ from fossil fuels (Rethink Priorities). The conversion values every tonne for its heat deaths (discounted over the decades until they come) and adds "Deaths caused by one more tonne of CO₂"'s air-pollution part times this row, at once. Here it is 0: trees taking up carbon leave the fuel burned elsewhere unchanged.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for a UK charity that both delivers services and funds others: a little under half the cost is staff. Our judgment; we haven't seen this charity's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: UK charity staff earn somewhat less than in comparable private-sector jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂ taken up per dollar donated
rows.explainer: The figure per dollar above; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest). The site turns these tonnes into years of healthy life through the deaths they avoid: "Deaths caused by one more tonne of CO₂", its heat part discounted over "Years until the heat deaths from a tonne of CO₂" for every tonne, and its air-pollution part, at once, times "Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne" above. SoGive notes that carbon taken up by trees is not the same as emissions avoided (it returns if the woodland is lost, and SoGive's survey of academics put 2 to more than 10 tonnes taken up as worth one avoided); the site treats them alike, which flatters planting.
